title: 3D Printing
desc: Learn to design, slice, print, finish and cost 3D-printed parts safely and sell them honestly.
outcomes: Prepare a model and slice it.
Print and finish a useful part.
task: Design or select a part, print it, finish it, test it against a requirement and cost it for sale.
condition: Access to a printer (own, makerspace or partner), a computer, free software, two peers and a mentor.
standard: Part meets the dimensions within 0.3 mm; print log shows settings; failure analysis written; safety rules followed; cost per part shown; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Makers, students, product designers, small manufacturers.
evidence: model, slicer settings, print log, test record, cost sheet
modules: Plastics: PLA, PETG, ABS; resins need care.
A bracket printed on its side is stronger.
Ventilation; do not touch hot parts.
Never leave long prints unattended without safeguards.
A smoke alarm and a fire blanket nearby.
Change one setting at a time.
Material, power, machine time, labour, failures.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: 3D home building, smart apparel, product design.
local: Product-safety and IP rules differ by place; do not copy protected designs.
ladder: Printers and materials

L1: learner can name printer types. Focus module: Printers and materials (Understand, 3 h). Know the options. Key points: Filament (fused) and resin printers. Plastics: PLA, PETG, ABS; resins need care. Match material to use.

Teach: open with the worked example. PLA is easy; PETG tougher. Then set the activity: Compare materials. Mark against the standard: Table. Check at this level: Easy filament? Model answer: PLA. Types.
Design for printing
L2: learner knows safety. Focus module: Design for printing (Apply, 4 h). Print-friendly shapes. Key points: Wall thickness, overhangs, tolerances. Orientation matters for strength. Add chamfers.

Teach: open with the worked example. A bracket printed on its side is stronger. Then set the activity: Design a part. Mark against the standard: Dimensions listed. Check at this level: Overhang fix? Model answer: Supports. Safety.
Slicing
L3: learner can slice. Focus module: Slicing (Apply, 4 h). Settings. Key points: Layer height, infill, speed, supports. Preview the path. Save settings.

Teach: open with the worked example. 0.2 mm layers with 20% infill. Then set the activity: Slice your part. Mark against the standard: Preview checked. Check at this level: Resin safety? Model answer: Gloves and eye protection. Slice.
Printing and safety

L4: learner can print. Focus module: Printing and safety (Apply, 4 h). Hot, moving, fumes. Key points: Ventilation; do not touch hot parts. Never leave long prints unattended without safeguards. Resin: gloves and eye protection.

Teach: open with the worked example. A smoke alarm and a fire blanket nearby. Then set the activity: Print and log. Mark against the standard: Log complete. Check at this level: Why ventilate? Model answer: Fumes. Print.
Troubleshooting
L5: learner can fix and cost. Focus module: Troubleshooting (Analyse, 3 h). Fix failures. Key points: Warping, stringing, poor adhesion, clogs. Change one setting at a time. Keep notes.

Teach: open with the worked example. A heated bed fixes warping. Then set the activity: Fix two issues. Mark against the standard: Notes recorded. Check at this level: Warping fix? Model answer: Heated bed. Fix.
Testing
L6: learner can lead a lab. Focus module: Testing (Evaluate, 3 h). Does it work? Key points: Dimension check with calipers. Load test within safe limits. Document.
Teach: open with the worked example. The bracket holds 5 kg. Then set the activity: Test. Mark against the standard: Record. Check at this level: Measuring tool? Model answer: Calipers. Lead.
Cost and sale
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Cost and sale (Create, 3 h). Price honestly. Key points: Material, power, machine time, labour, failures. Quote per part. Disclose limits.

Teach: open with the worked example. Cost 62 INR; price 150 INR. Then set the activity: Cost it. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Costs? Model answer: Material, power, time, labour, failures. Peer audit.
